content: I removed the tensioners to give more room. Quoting numbers of teeth isn't helpful because depending on your route (Gen2 vs Non) the belt teeth are different. It would be better to line them up with a marker on the mount, or the edge of the mount so that the end of the belt aligns with the edge of the mount and you know these's enough overlap. Thats what I did and I'll see if that causes a problem. Belt is tensioned and runs OK. Time and printing will tell.

Dear Prusa representatives, please consider
1. suggest temporarily undoing the tensioners to people coming from the Gen2 upgrade
2. write two documentations instead of mixing the gen2  upgrade with indx
3. rewrite the section so that you work on "lower belt first, upper belt later" rather than right then left.
3. lengthening the belts a bit more and use consistent teeth indications.
4. adding a new 3d printed part that keeps lower belts in place while you work on the upper ones

I cannot stress how important this step is to get right. If you don't get enough teeth through, the belt can come out during the tensioning process later. Now I have to take a bunch of my printer apart to reattach the belts...

I would attach the belts to the head plate BEFORE attaching the tensioners to the front of the printer to ensure you get enough slack on the ends to hold the belt in place.

Correct me if I am wrong.
I assume this is for GT2 belts so since GT2 have a pitch of 2mm. 
4.5 x 2 = 9mm (taking average of 4-5 teeth)
9 / 1.5 = 6mm or 6 teeth (1.5 pitch of GT1.5 belt)
Same for the  other belt 
6-7 teeth for GT2 translates to 8 or 9 teeth for GT1.5
6-7 Gen 1 belt teeth? Because the Gen 2 belts have more teeth. Is this why my printer can’t even do a x axis test? This step is confusing with 4-5 or 6-7
I think my belts were too short, there was definitely not enough to get both routed out with 4-5 teeth protruding on each side
The first picture of this is so weird why not just have it facing the normal way instead of having to invert it after doing that initial step?

Inserting the belts is super hard when the tentioner idlers are already screwed in. I think it would be easier to change the order here and fix the head mouting plate first and than fix the tentioners. This is how i also did it when assembling the core one already since i couldn't get it to work otherwise.
Great move undoing the tensioners.  It made inserting the belts a breeze

replies.content: Agreed. Made it much easier. I also used small C clamps to hold the belts in place. Freed up my hands.

Indeed. I did put one side in, then released both tensioners completely.
Put the other side of the belts in and screw the plate into place. Once that is done, put the tensioners back.

content: If you have the tensioner screws attached to the pulleys loosen or remove the screws. You will attach the screws to the pulley in step 12.

replies.content: Yep doing this without undoing the tensioners we had to do in a previous step for the indx + 2 upgrade was impossible for me

I found it helpful to secure the right side with a cable tie while working on the left side.
Before you insert the belt, insert the nuts into the head mounting plate now in the notch
